 U.S. midterm elections 2026 LIVE: VP Vance says Iran war was the reason Republicans lost midterms
 Democrats won full control of the U.S. Congress in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party
 Updated - November 04, 2026 10:25 pm IST 
 The Hindu Bureau READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Vice President JD Vance arrives on Air Force Two on November 2, 2026, at Joint Base Andrews, Md.
 | Photo Credit: 
 AP
 U .S. Vice-President JD Vance said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that the Iran war was the reason Republicans lost the midterm elections, as he sought to distance himself from the conflict ahead of a possible 2028 White House run.
 Democrats won full control of the U.S. Congress in a sweeping midterm rout on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.
 Also read: U.S. Midterm Election night agenda: When polls close and when to expect results 
 The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Mr. Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Mr. Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular President.
 Also read: Trump’s Republicans scramble to stop Democratic midterms wave 
 Mr. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times : “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats.”
 Follow LIVE updates here Key Updates
 U.S. Senate results map 
 November 04, 2026 21:50 Democrat has a narrow lead in uncalled race for Kansas governor Democrat Cindy Holscher has a lead of less than a percentage point over Republican Ty Masterson in the Kansas governor’s race.
 Holscher’s 5,557-vote lead, with an estimated 98% of votes counted, comes after Democrat Adam Hamilton became the first member of his party to win a Senate seat in nearly a century.
 Both Holscher and Masterson serve in the state Senate, where the latter serves as its president.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 21:46 U.S. VP Vance says Iran war was ‘the reason’ Republicans lost midterms U.S. Vice-President JD Vance said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that the Iran war was the reason Republicans lost the midterm elections, as he sought to distance himself from the conflict ahead of a possible 2028 White House run.
 Read more here 
 November 04, 2026 21:35 Abdul El-Sayed: The progressive’s progress In a country where, for more than a quarter of a century, the word “Muslim” has been used as an accusation in politics, Abdul El-Sayed’s election as the first Muslim member of the U.S. Senate breaks perhaps the thickest of glass ceilings in American public life. Dr. El-Sayed, a physician and epidemiologist, defeated the Republican former Congressman Mike Rogers with 52.5% of the vote, seven percentage points ahead of his rival.
 Read the story here: Abdul El-Sayed: The progressive’s progress
 Abdul El-Sayed becomes the first Muslim U.S. Senator, reshaping Michigan and progressive politics amid heavy outside spending and debated Israel stance.
 November 04, 2026 21:27 Abdul El-Sayed expresses pride in name Trump tried to weaponize In his victory speech in Michigan’s Senate race, Abdul El-Sayed used the middle name Trump often invoked while telling voters they should fear the progressive Democrat.
 “My name is Abdulrahman Mohamed Sayed, and I am so proud and honored to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan,” he said.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 21:02 Mike Johnson won’t seek reelection as House Republican leader after Democratic takeover House Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek election as House Republican leader following the Democrats’ win. That’s according to a person who spoke on condition of anonymity to disclose the plans.
 Democrats are riding their sweep of Congress into a new era. They’re eager to meet voter demands for change with plans to tackle high costs of living and confront President Donald Trump’s final years in the White House.
 The results of today’s midterm elections set up a moment of divided government. Democrats ousted Republicans from coast to coast and in many surprising places in between. Voters rejected the president’s party for the promise of something different.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 21:00 Amid concern about costs, lower-income voters move toward Democrats In a year when economic concerns drove many voters’ choices, lower-income voters shifted toward the Democrats.
 More than half of voters with a 2025 household income less than $50,000 voted for the Democratic candidate in their local U.S. House race. These voters were about evenly split between Mr. Trump and Ms. Harris in 2024. About 3 in 10 U.S. voters nationally report having a family income under $50,000 each year.
 The survey suggests these voters were more likely than voters with a higher income to say they were concerned about the costs of food, groceries, gas and utilities.
 - AP 
 November 04, 2026 20:57 Democrats usher in a new era with their resounding sweep of the House and the Senate
 Democrats are riding their sweep of Congress into a new era, eager to meet voter demands for change with plans to tackle high living costs and confront Trump’s final years in the White House.
 In a nationwide romp, Democrats ousted Republicans from coast to coast, with many surprising places in between, as voters rejected the president’s party for the promise of something different. Democrats’ majorities will be padded by wide margins in both the House and the Senate.
 The results set up a divided government, with Congress poised to reassert itself as a coequal branch ready to challenge Trump and reverse course after two years of unified GOP control.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 20:13 U.S. midterm results may matter less for India-U.S. ties than for India’s room to manoeuvre in geopolitics
 The dramatic results of the U.S. midterms will probably have less impact on India-U.S. bilateral relations than on geopolitics and, as a result, India’s “operating environment” in the world. 
 The elections are likely to hand Democrats a sizable majority in the House of Representatives and a comfortable edge in the Senate, which means U.S. President Donald Trump will face restraints on both domestic and foreign policy. Here are five areas where this will matter most to India.
 Read the story here: U.S. midterm results may matter less for India-U.S. ties than for India’s room to manoeuvre in geopolitics
 The U.S. midterm results may matter less for India-U.S. ties than for geopolitics, from the Iran war and Russian oil to trade talks and the Quad.
 November 04, 2026 19:53 Democrats win five governor races as Hinojosa, Bottoms, Haaland make history Democrats are on track for big gains in governor races, notching victories in Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Georgia and Wisconsin, according to U.S. media projections, with a number of other races still too early to call as of early Wednesday.
 Three candidates made history. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms became the country’s first Black woman elected governor. 
 In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa became the first Latina governor in the state’s history, unseating a well-financed Republican incumbent in a historically conservative state. And in New Mexico, Democrat Deb Haaland became the country’s first female Native American governor.
 Read the story here: U.S. Midterm election Democrats win five governor races as Hinojosa, Bottoms, Haaland make history
 Democrats win governor races in Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Iowa and Wisconsin, with Gina Hinojosa, Keisha Lance Bottoms and Deb Haaland making history, Reuters reports.
 November 04, 2026 19:48 Governor seats also see a wave of historic firsts after U.S. midterm elections Across the country, states elected a wave of governors who are the first Black, Latina or female leaders of their respective states.
 Maryland Gov. Wes Moore, the only current Black governor, ​ won reelection ​ on Tuesday. Republican Byron Donalds in Florida and Democrat David Crowley in Wisconsin were elected as the first Black governors in their states.
 Latino Democrats also will take on the highest state office in two of the biggest states. Texas voters rejected Republican Gov. Greg Abbott in favor of Gina Hinojosa, who will be the state’s first Latina governor.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 19:47 Speaker Mike Johnson says GOP will keep working ‘to make America great again’ “While the outcome of this midterm is not what we’d hoped and fought for, a new battle is just beginning,” the Republican speaker said overnight on social media.
 Johnson is expected to face a challenge from Republican rivals if he tries to stay on as GOP leader in the new Congress, which Democrats will control after the midterm rout. He did not immediately address his plans.
 - AP 
 November 04, 2026 18:09 Iranian officials say midterm results show U.S. voters have rejected Trump’s war Iranian targets hit ahead of the midterms Iran marks anniversary of 1979 seizure of U.S. Embassy Back-channel negotiations continue
 Iranian officials on Wednesday celebrated U.S. voters’ rebuke of the Republican Party and President Donald Trump in the midterm elections, as the region waited to see how the results could affect the Iran war.
 Concerns about the war’s effects, particularly frustration over rising prices for fuel and other goods in the U.S., helped Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s vote.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 18:02 Democrat David Crowley defeats Trump loyalist to become Wisconsin’s first Black governor
 Democrat David Crowley defeated a Republican with close ties to President Donald Trump on Tuesday, rising from a childhood in one of the nation’s poorest neighborhoods to become the first Black person to lead the battleground state.
 Crowley’s win over U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany marks the first time in Wisconsin’s 178-year history that Democrats will hold the governor’s office for more than eight consecutive years. He will replace Gov. Tony Evers, who decided to retire instead of seeking a third term.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 17:23 ‘A new era in world relations,’ says Cyril Ramaphosa South African President Cyril Ramaphosa says the Democrats taking control of the House and the Senate in the U.S. midterms is going to “introduce a new era in world relations.”
 Ramaphosa says he hopes South Africa will be able to improve its bilateral relationship with the United States after his country became a target for criticism during President Donald Trump’s second term.
 Trump’s Republican administration has made several moves against South Africa’s government, which he has baselessly accused of discriminating against its white minority.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 16:22 Democratic victories cloud outlook for AI data centre rollout Strong wins for Democratic candidates threaten the prospects for energy-guzzling data centres in key U.S. states, potentially slowing the AI rollout that has carried Wall Street forward over the past four years.
 After a campaign marked by growing concerns about the environmental impacts of data centres popping up across the United States, President Donald Trump -- an enthusiastic backer of hands-off regulation for what he calls “super intelligence” -- endured a stinging rebuke of his Republican party.
 Democrats gained key strongholds such as Texas, where both the Senate and governorship were won by candidates backing greater data centre regulation.
 -AFP 
 November 04, 2026 15:45 U.S. midterm elections impact on India: Faster trade deal talks and higher tariffs likely The results of the U.S. midterm elections, which show that the Democrats have gained control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, will likely speed up talks between India and the U.S. on a trade deal but could also see higher tariffs on India until the deal is closed, according to experts.
 On the one hand, a desire to now quickly close the trade deal to show strength domestically could induce Mr. Trump to increase his tariff pressure on India, while on the other, Indian negotiators will likely see this election result as an opportunity to push through a favourable deal for India.
 Read the story here 
 ​ U.S. midterm elections impact on India: faster trade deal talks and higher tariffs likely
 U.S. midterms may speed India-U.S. trade talks but risk higher tariffs, as Trump pressures for a quick deal despite Congress shift.
 ​
 November 04, 2026 15:21 Democrat Aaron Ford wins election for Governor in Nevada Democrat Aaron Ford won the election as Governor of Nevada, defeating Republican incumbent Joe Lombardo.
 Mr. Ford, the attorney general, defeated the incumbent Mr. Lombardo in what was considered one of the country’s most competitive governor’s races. 
 Mr. Ford ran with the backing of the Democratic congressional delegation, California Gov. Gavin Newsom and former Vice-President Kamala Harris.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 15:15 Far-right wave 'unravelling', says Spain's Sanchez after U.S. vote The global far-right is “unravelling”, Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on Wednesday (November 4) as he celebrated the Democrat victory in U.S. elections which saw them seize control of Congress in a rebuke to President Donald Trump.
 “It happened in Brazil. It just happened in the US. And it will soon happen in Spain,” Mr. Sanchez, who is a global progressive star but whose premiership is in peril in snap elections he called for November 29. The far-right wave of his rivals is “no longer growing, it is unravelling,” he added.
 -AFP 
 November 04, 2026 15:03 South African President: U.S. midterm results introduce new era in world relations South African ‌President Cyril Ramaphosa said ⁠on Wednesday (November 4) that the ‌results from midterm elections ‌in ‌the ⁠United ⁠States will “introduce a new era ‌in world relations”.
 “We have seen that the ‌Democrats have taken control ⁠of the Senate and ‌of the House, and the people of ‌America have spoken,” Mr. Ramaphosa told reporters.
 -Reuters 
 November 04, 2026 15:02 Democrat Susie Lee wins reelection to U.S. House in Nevada’s 3rd Congressional District Democrat Susie Lee won the reelection to the U.S. House of Representatives representing Nevada’s 3rd Congressional District, defeating Republican Marty O’Donnell.
 Ms. Lee won a fifth term representing Nevada’s most competitive district that includes part of metro Las Vegas and rural Clark County and which President Donald Trump won in 2024.
 First elected in 2018, Ms. Lee campaigned as a moderate and highlighted her bipartisan record. She has been frequently targeted by Republicans.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 14:33 Voters back abortion rights, reject Trump's redistricting in state ballot measures Abortion-rights advocates notched victories in Missouri and Virginia on Tuesday (November 3), and voters delivered a double dose of disapproval to President Donald Trump’s redistricting efforts as they decided 145 ballot questions in more than three dozen states.
 The ballot measures provided a political undercard for a high-profile midterm election that was determining which party controls Congress, state legislatures and gubernatorial offices in many states.
 Some measures put Mr. Trump’s priorities to a public test by gauging support for his attempts to redraw congressional districts, limit transgender athletes in sports and strengthen voter identification requirements.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 14:22 Democrat Tina Kotek wins reelection for Governor in Oregon Democrat Tina Kotek won the reelection as Governor of Oregon, defeating Republican Christine Drazan. 
 Ms. Kotek, the incumbent Governor, previously served as Oregon’s House speaker and has frequently sparred with President Donald Trump’s administration. She campaigned on a pledge to tackle homelessness, mental health and education. 
 She defeated Ms. Drazan, a Republican state senator, for a second time; the two also faced off in 2022. 
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 14:00 Republican Pete Ricketts wins reelection to U.S. Senate from Nebraska Republican Pete Ricketts won the reelection to the U.S. Senate representing Nebraska, defeating independent candidate Dan Osborn. 
 Mr. Ricketts will now serve his first full six-year term, following his 2023 appointment to replace Republican Sen. Ben Sasse and 2024 special election victory. 
 Mr. Osborn, an industrial mechanic and military veteran, also ran in 2024 against the state’s other Republican senator, Deb Fischer.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 13:59 U.S. administration remains same after Democrat victory, Berlin says German Defence Minister ‌Boris Pistorius on Wednesday (November 4) ⁠congratulated U.S. Democrats on a “historic victory” ‌in Congress, while ‌noting ‌the ⁠U.S. administration ⁠will remain the same and Berlin will ‌continue trustfully cooperating with it.
 Speaking at the ‌Berlin Security Conference, Mr. Pistorius added he did ⁠not know what ‌President Donald Trump’s plans for the near future looked ‌like but that Berlin would reach ⁠out to both Democrats ⁠and Republicans.
 -Reuters 
 November 04, 2026 13:52 Democrat Katie Hobbs wins reelection for Governor in Arizona Democrat Katie Hobbs won the reelecton as Governor of Arizona, defeating Republican Andy Biggs, Republican Gertritrude Gonzalez (write-in) and Republican Alice Novoa (write-in). 
 Ms. Hobbs won despite being viewed as the most vulnerable Democratic Governor in the country. She courted disaffected Republicans and independent voters to win a second term in the swing state.
 Hobbs also picked a former Republican, former Mesa mayor John Giles, as her running mate.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 13:44 Nevada’s last voter casts a ballot 5 hours after polls close Nevada didn’t release its first batch of results until midnight — five hours after polls closed.
 In accordance with state law, results are not released until the last voter has cast a ballot. The polls closed at 7 p.m. PST, but election locations saw longer than normal wait times due to a large turnout, as well as an extra step in the election process. 
 The last voter finished before midnight, the Nevada secretary of state’s office announced.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 13:42 Democrat Richard Pan wins election to U.S. House in California’s 6th Congressional District Democrat Richard Pan won the election on Wednesday (November 4) to the U.S. House of Representatives representing California’s 6th Congressional District. 
 Mr. Pan is a doctor and former state senator. As a legislator, he became a target of the anti-vaccine movement after sponsoring a bill to eliminate philosophical and religious exemptions for school immunization requirements.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 13:39 Republican candidate criticised for racist post concedes defeat in a Texas election Republican candidate Bo French, who faced widespread criticism on social media over his racist posts, has conceded defeat in the Texas Railroad Commissioner election to Democrat Jon Rosenthal.
 French faced backlash after posting an image of an event at a Texas university showing a gathering of predominantly South Asian people, including Indians.
 “I heard UT graduation this year looked like this. I didn’t believe it. The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined,” he posted on social media in September.
 -PTI 
 November 04, 2026 13:29 Republican Jim Pillen wins reelection for Governor in Nebraska Republican Jim Pillen won the election as Governor of Nebraska, defeating Democrat Lynne Walz. Pillen, the incumbent Governor who is also a hog farm owner, first assumed office in 2023. 
 Mr. Walz is a former state senator.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 13:28 Republican Kurt Alme wins election to U.S. Senate from Montana Republican Kurt Alme won the election to the U.S. Senate representing Montana, defeating independent Seth Bodnar and Democrat Alani Bankhead. Alme will replace Republican Sen. 
 Steve Daines, who made a surprise announcement in March, just ahead of the state’s filing deadline, that he would not run for a third term.
 Mr. Alme’s win comes after a three-way contest with Mr. Bodnar, a former University of Montana president, and Mr. Bankhead, a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel who refused to drop out as Mr. Bodnar hoped to clear the field against Mr. Alme.
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 13:27 Indian-American Ami Bera wins U.S. House from California Indian-American Democratic lawmaker Ami Bera has won reelection to U.S. House in California’s 3rd Congressional District, defeating Republican Robb Tucker.
 Mr. Bera, 61, won his eighth term in the U.S. House of Representatives.
 Physician-turned-politician Amerish Babulal ‘Ami’ Bera is the longest-serving Indian American in the U.S. Congress and is considered a strong voice on healthcare and diplomacy.
 -PTI 
 November 04, 2026 13:25 Democrat Andrews' South Carolina midterm victory defies prediction markets odds Prediction markets notched their first high-profile miss of Tuesday’s (November 3) U.S. midterm elections, as Democrat Annie Andrews ousted Republican Darline Graham to unexpectedly win ‌a U.S. Senate seat in conservative South Carolina.
 Prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket had ⁠implied a 70% chance of Ms. Graham, the sister of the late U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham, winning that race as ‌of late afternoon Tuesday.
 Ms. Andrews, a pediatrician, is the first Democrat to win a Senate ‌seat in South Carolina in 28 years. ‌Republican ⁠President Donald Trump carried South Carolina by ⁠18 percentage points just two years ago, and neither Democrats nor Republicans considered the race to be competitive until recent weeks.
 -Reuters 
 _South Carolina US Senate final vote share 2026@2x.jpeg
 November 04, 2026 13:15 Former MLB star Mark Teixeira wins House seat in Texas Mark Teixeira, a former World Series champion, is headed to Congress.
 The slugger-turned-Republican politician will represent Texas’ 21st Congressional District in Washington after defeating Democrat Kristin ‌Hook in the Tuesday(November 3) mid-term election.
 Mr. Teixeira was leading with more than 54% of the ⁠vote after 95% of the ballots had been counted, according to multiple media reports.
 Mr. Teixeira tweeted, “Tonight’s victory belongs to ‌the people of Texas’s 21st District. I’m not going to Washington for myself, but ‌rather to be a strong, responsive voice for ‌every ⁠family in this district.
 -Reuters 
 November 04, 2026 13:02 China 'willing to continue working' with U.S. after midterms China said on Wednesday (November 4) it was “willing to continue working” with the United States following midterm elections that saw President Donald Trump’s Republicans lose control of both chambers of Congress.
 “The midterm elections are an internal affair of the United States. China is willing to continue working with the U.S. to uphold and implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, strengthen communication, properly manage differences, expand cooperation, and build a constructive, strategically stable China-U.S. relationship based on the principles of respect, fairness, and reciprocity,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a regular briefing.
 -AFP 
 November 04, 2026 12:54 Elon Musk jokes about GOP election defeat after spending record sums on party Elon Musk, who spent record sums on Republicans, joked about the party’s midterm election defeat to Democrats on Wednesday (November 4).
 “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time,” Mr. Musk, who contributed nearly half a billion dollars to Republican political efforts, said on X.
 Here’s the story 
 U.S. midterm elections: Musk jokes about GOP election defeat after spending record sums on party
 Elon Musk jokes about GOP defeat after spending hundreds of millions to aid Republicans as Democrats seize Congress in 2026.
 November 04, 2026 12:41 Democrats win U.S. House and take unified control of Congress Democrats have won control of the U.S. House in addition to the U.S. Senate, delivering a shockingly decisive rebuke of Republican governance in Washington and ushering in a new era of congressional resistance to President Donald Trump.
 The midterm elections channeled voters’ deep frustrations over high prices, the Iran war and concerns over government corruption. Democrats routed their rivals across the map, from Texas to Iowa to New Hampshire, including states Mr. Trump won by double digits just two years ago.
 Democratic control will profoundly reshape Mr. Trump’s final two years in office and likely hamstring his agenda. 
 -AP 
 November 04, 2026 12:37 Democrat Abdul El-Sayed claims victory in Michigan Senate battle Democrat Abdul El-Sayed said early on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that he had won a U.S. Senate seat in Michigan over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, which would make him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.
 “Michigan, we did it!” Mr. El-Sayed said in a speech at his election headquarters in Detroit.
 “I am so proud and honoured to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.”
 Read the story here 
 Democrat Abdul El-Sayed claims victory in Michigan Senate battle
 Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate seat, becoming first Muslim in the U.S. Senate and pledging healthcare reform and overturning money in politics.
 November 04, 2026 12:30 Numbers that tell the story of the Democrats' midterm blowout Total turnout numbers were not in yet, but Americans cast more than 61.7 million votes even before election day, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab.
 Total spending for the 2026 midterms soared to a record $11.9 billion, substantially higher than the $8.9 billion racked up in 2022, according to OpenSecrets, a non-partisan authority on spending in U.S. politics.
 Ninety-four years ago was the last time Kansas sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate. But on Tuesday (November 3) night, Adam Hamilton unseated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall.
 Texas also went blue for the first time in decades, with Mr. Talarico scoring a massive upset to flip a Senate seat in the Lone Star State for the first since 1988 -- the year before Mr. Talarico was born.
 It showed in NBC News exit polls, when Latino voters backed Democratic candidates by 62% to 35% over Republicans.
 -AFP 
 November 04, 2026 12:27 Trump congratulates Democrats on midterms, says Iran war played role
 President Donald Trump had rare praise for rival Democrats on Tuesday (November 3) after their stunning U.S. midterm elections victory and admitted the Iran war may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party.
 But the 80-year-old refused to take any personal responsibility for the result that upends the final two years of his presidency, instead trying to shift the blame to his fellow Republicans.
 With polls showing the Iran war and resulting rise in oil prices was vastly unpopular with voters, Mr. Trump also acknowledged that the stalled conflict had contributed to the result.
 “I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I’ve done with Iran,” Mr. Trump told Fox .
 Yet Mr. Trump’s conciliatory tone did not extend to his own party.
 -AFP 
 November 04, 2026 12:18 "American people sent a clear message today", says former U.S. President Barack Obama “Tonight, the American people sent a clear message — they want a politics that brings people together rather than divides them, and leaders who offer concrete solutions to the challenges they face,” former U.S. President Barack Obama said, reacting to the Democrats’ sweeping victory over the Senate in Tuesday’s (November 3) midterm elections. 
 “While this administration has another two years in office, our job now is to roll up our sleeves, make changes wherever we have the power to do so, prevent further damage, and lay the groundwork for the future,” he added. 
 ​ ​
 November 04, 2026 12:08 Texas turns Blue: Democrats Talarico, Hinojosa topple Republicans Democrat James Talarico, a former schoolteacher and Presbyterian seminarian who campaigned on a “politics of love,” on Tuesday (November 3) won the U.S. Senate race in Texas, dealing a historic blow to Republicans that could reshape American politics.
 In another political earthquake for the deeply conservative southern border state, Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseated incumbent Texas Governor Greg Abbott.
 -AFP 
 Texas US Senate final vote share 2026@2x.jpeg
 November 04, 2026 12:03 They did a good job: Trump on Democrats' midterm victory U.S. President Donald Trump congratulated Democrats for doing “a good job” after the party clinched victory in the midterm elections.
 Mr. Trump, in a call with CBS News , said that his message is “congratulations to the Democrats, and I look forward to working with you for the good of our country.”
 He said that he “wasn’t on the ballot, and there was nothing that could be done about that.”
 “If I was, we would have won,” he added.
 -PTI 
 November 04, 2026 11:58 Hakeem Jeffries poised to become speaker of U.S. House of Representatives The Democrats’ midterm election win puts Hakeem Jeffries in line to become the first Black speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives, with the dual challenge of opposing President ‌Donald Trump while bridging the gap between his party’s moderates and its more vocal progressives.
 As speaker, Mr. Jeffries, representing a New York City congressional district, would preside over a majority that will be sworn in the first week of January, taking the reins from Republicans ⁠who controlled the House for the past four years.
 Here’s the full story 
 Hakeem Jeffries poised to become first Black Speaker of U.S. House of Representatives
